newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk rate case extansion sought.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk rate case extansion sought.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp and the New York Department of Public Service staff have jointly asked to extend by another 30 days the utility's 1997 rate request proceedings so parties can continue to focus on issues related to its PowerChoice proposal, the company said.
Three previous extensions of the case have been granted.

As with the other extensions, this would "allow the parties participating in various aspects of the PowerChoice negotiations additional time to pursure a vialbe long-term solution to the issues facing Niagara Mohawk," the company and the staff said in their request.
Such a solution might eliminate the need for the rate increase, the letter to Public Service Commission Administrative Law Judge William Bouteiller said.
At issue is the continuing talks with independent power producers, Niaraga Mohawk spokeswoman Kerry Burns said.
Earlier this month, the company said it remained hopeful of reaching an agreement with these operators of unregulated generating plants.

PowerChoice, Niagara Mohawk's proposal to create a competitive electricity market, was put forward in October 1995. In February, the company filed an 8.4 rate increase to become effective January 1, 1997, if PowerChoice is not adopted.
If granted, it said, the newest extension would change the effective date of the requested rate increase to July 11, 1997.
